topic.title: The free trial is priced on forgetting
topic.claim: A free trial isn't priced on the people who love the product. It's priced on the people who forget to cancel.
topic.moment: A ₹499 debit in month three for an app you opened twice.

turn.believed: Trials let you test before you pay.
turn.actually: Trials work best for the company when you don't remember them.

topic.villain: Auto-renew subscriptions with cancel buttons buried three screens deep
topic.because: Auto-pay on UPI or card means silence counts as yes. Every forgotten trial is revenue with no service cost.
topic.payoff: Open your UPI autopay list tonight. Count the ones you'd sign up for again today.
topic.behaviour: Apps ask for a mandate up front, then make cancelling harder than joining.
topic.group: Anyone with three or more subscriptions
topic.send_to: The sibling who pays for four OTT apps
topic.why_now: UPI autopay has made signing up one tap and cancelling a hunt.

score.why: A free trial is priced on the people who forget to cancel. The UPI autopay check is a test readers will actually do tonight.

mechanism.broken_premise: None of the premises is false. Saying trials are 'priced on' people who forget to cancel, and that the app is 'betting' they won't remember, is an interpretation of business motive. It is not a claim that can be shown untrue. The factual premises check out. Under UPI AutoPay you sign a mandate with your PIN and later debits run without any further action from you. India's 2023 CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines do name 'subscription trap', and that definition covers asking for auto-debit authorisation for a free subscription and hiding the cancel option. One thing slides 4–5 leave out: by rule, the bank sends a notice 24 hours before each scheduled debit, and you can tap it to pause or cancel. Any mandate can also be revoked from the AutoPay list in GPay or PhonePe without opening the merchant's app. So stopping a charge doesn't depend only on your memory, though if you don't act, the debit still goes through.
mechanism.actual_mechanism: A UPI AutoPay mandate is authorised once with your UPI PIN, and after that the merchant can debit you on schedule. Before each debit, the bank must send a notice at least 24 hours ahead, and you can pause or revoke the mandate from it. You can also revoke from the AutoPay section of your UPI app, after which the merchant can't debit you again. India's CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines (30 Nov 2023) list 'subscription trap' as a banned practice. It covers making cancellation impossible or long, hiding the cancel option, forcing payment details or auto-debit authorisation for a free subscription, and unclear cancellation instructions.

_ledger.text:
[cover] A free trial is priced on the people who [forget to cancel]
The fans would have paid anyway. The money is somewhere else.
 

[slide 1] A free trial isn't priced on people who love the app. It's priced on people who forget to cancel.

[slide 2] Your phone buzzes in month three: ₹499 debited, for an app you opened twice and forgot you even had.
And the first person you blame is yourself.

[slide 3] Before the free trial even starts, the app asks you to set up UPI autopay. One tap on GPay or PhonePe, your PIN, done.

[slide 4] Because with autopay, silence counts as yes.
Paying needs nothing from you. To stop, you have to remember, and the app is betting you won't.

[slide 5] Three forgotten apps at ₹149, ₹299 and ₹499 come to ₹947 a month.
That's ₹11,364 a year, for apps you never open.

[slide 6] So the trial was never really a trial. It runs on everyone who meant to cancel and didn't.
Call it the forgetting fee.

[slide 7] India's 2023 dark pattern guidelines even have a name for this. A "subscription trap."
Making you approve auto-debit for a free trial counts. So does hiding the cancel button.

[slide 8] You signed up for one series, or maybe a match, or a month of workouts, and then life moved on. The mandate didn't.
Call it careless if you want. The app planned for it.

[slide 9] Open your UPI autopay list tonight and count the ones you'd sign up for again today.
Every app after that number is billing you for being busy.

[end card] Come back to this the next time an app says "Start free trial" and asks for your UPI PIN.
Send to the sibling who pays for four OTT apps and watches one.

[caption] Somewhere in your autopay list is a logo you won't recognise.

[alt text] Text carousel arguing that free trials make money from people who forget to cancel. UPI autopay mandates make signing up one tap, and silence counts as yes. Three forgotten apps at ₹149, ₹299 and ₹499 cost ₹947 a month, or ₹11,364 a year. India's 2023 dark pattern guidelines call this a subscription trap. Ends by asking readers to open their UPI autopay list and count the subscriptions they would still choose today.

e2bb8c8bdab4e135e962cbdc9a1582d618c3f1a9.broken_premise: None of the premises is false. Saying trials are 'priced on' people who forget to cancel, and that the app is 'betting' they won't remember, is an interpretation of business motive. It is not a claim that can be shown untrue. The factual premises check out. Under UPI AutoPay you sign a mandate with your PIN and later debits run without any further action from you. India's 2023 CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines do name 'subscription trap', and that definition covers asking for auto-debit authorisation for a free subscription and hiding the cancel option. One thing slides 4–5 leave out: by rule, the bank sends a notice 24 hours before each scheduled debit, and you can tap it to pause or cancel. Any mandate can also be revoked from the AutoPay list in GPay or PhonePe without opening the merchant's app. So stopping a charge doesn't depend only on your memory, though if you don't act, the debit still goes through.
e2bb8c8bdab4e135e962cbdc9a1582d618c3f1a9.actual_mechanism: A UPI AutoPay mandate is authorised once with your UPI PIN, and after that the merchant can debit you on schedule. Before each debit, the bank must send a notice at least 24 hours ahead, and you can pause or revoke the mandate from it. You can also revoke from the AutoPay section of your UPI app, after which the merchant can't debit you again. India's CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines (30 Nov 2023) list 'subscription trap' as a banned practice. It covers making cancellation impossible or long, hiding the cancel option, forcing payment details or auto-debit authorisation for a free subscription, and unclear cancellation instructions.

cover.headline: A free trial is priced on the people who [forget to cancel]
cover.sub: The fans would have paid anyway. The money is somewhere else.

paragraphs: A free trial isn't priced on people who love the app. It's priced on people who forget to cancel.
slides.why_swipe: If not the fans, then who is paying for it?

paragraphs: Your phone buzzes in month three: ₹499 debited, for an app you opened twice and forgot you even had.
And the first person you blame is yourself.
slides.why_swipe: How did it get that far without you noticing?

paragraphs: Before the free trial even starts, the app asks you to set up UPI autopay. One tap on GPay or PhonePe, your PIN, done.
slides.why_swipe: Why does the app want that one tap so badly?

paragraphs: Because with autopay, silence counts as yes.
Paying needs nothing from you. To stop, you have to remember, and the app is betting you won't.
slides.why_swipe: How much does that forgetting actually cost?

paragraphs: Three forgotten apps at ₹149, ₹299 and ₹499 come to ₹947 a month.
That's ₹11,364 a year, for apps you never open.
slides.why_swipe: So what is the trial really for?

paragraphs: So the trial was never really a trial. It runs on everyone who meant to cancel and didn't.
slides.why_swipe: Is any of this even allowed?

paragraphs: India's 2023 dark pattern guidelines even have a name for this. A "subscription trap."
Making you approve auto-debit for a free trial counts. So does hiding the cancel button.
You signed up for one series, or maybe a match, or a month of workouts, and then life moved on. The mandate didn't.
Call it careless if you want. The app planned for it.
slides.why_swipe: What can you see for yourself, right now?

paragraphs: Open your UPI autopay list tonight and count the ones you'd sign up for again today.
Every app after that number is billing you for being busy.

end.save: Come back to this the next time an app says "Start free trial" and asks for your UPI PIN.
end.send: Send to the sibling who pays for four OTT apps and watches one.
end.promise: How brands really sell to India.

Three forgotten apps at ₹149, ₹299 and ₹499 cost ₹947 a month, or ₹11,364 a year. India's 2023 dark pattern guidelines call this a subscription trap. Ends by asking readers to open their UPI autopay list and count the subscriptions they would still choose today.
